analysis.title: US Equity Strategy & GVAT: Following AI's $1.6 trillion Money Trail: Mapping the Revenue Generated by the Capex Boom
key_insights: MS maps $1.6T of 2027 hyperscaler and neocloud AI capex to about $1.7T of supplier revenues across roughly 50 companies. The difference is attributed to private neoclouds and bitcoin miners, timing differences, and price increases in supplier revenue estimates not yet in capex estimates.

New lease capex estimates add about $195B to 2027 capex and $246B to 2028. Total AI capex is $980B in 2026 (+~100% y/y), $1.58T in 2027 (+~60% y/y) and $1.81T in 2028 (+14% y/y). Cash capex alone is $1.4T in 2027, so leases lift the total by 14%.

Hyperscalers disclose more than $1.1T of lease commitments signed but not yet commenced. Leased data centers bypass cash-flow capex and management capex guidance, so MS treats leases as synthetic capex.

MS tracks about 65% absorption of AI capex into S&P 500 revenue. This is $1.0T in 2027, or 4.9% of SPX sales, and about 24% of 2027 SPX sales growth. SPX sales growth is 8.6% with AI capex versus 6.6% without.
NVDA captures about 67% of the AI revenue absorbed by the S&P 500 in 2027, roughly $690B. Ex-NVDA flow-through is $339B, or 1.6% of SPX 2027 sales.

AI names in the S&P 500 (42 'Core to Thesis' names) grow 2027 sales 28% versus 5% for non-AI, and 2027 earnings 25% versus 4%. They drive 60% of 2027 SPX sales growth and 78% of 2027 earnings growth, and make up 37% of 2027 consensus net income.

Earnings growth appears near its peak. Both the AI and ex-AI cohorts peaked in 2Q26, and SPX net income growth falls from 36% in 2026 to 12% in 2027. MS expects leadership to shift from pure Enablers toward blended Enabler/Adopters and Adopters.

MS expects hyperscaler capex to add about 32 GW of compute in 2027 and 38 GW in 2028. Total compute capacity reaches roughly 125 GW by YE28, about 4x 2025. Custom ASICs rise from 34% of incremental capacity in 2025 to 66% in 2028.

MS sees 25-50% ROIC on GenAI spend across three models: a hyperscaler GPU rental business (about 25-40%), a model-enabled API on owned infrastructure (about 40%+, with 70%+ incremental EBIT margins) and an API on third-party infrastructure. The bank is bullish AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and META.

In a capex slowdown, MS sees two scenarios. In the bullish one, capital intensity moderates, FCF revisions are positive and the multiple re-rates. In the bearish one, returns disappoint, D&A deleverage hits earnings and the multiple de-rates. Hyperscalers generate about $1T of OCF in each of 2027 and 2028.

In semis, Joseph Moore expects hyperscaler spend to keep accruing to large caps, led by NVDA as revenue per GW scales (toward $40bn per the summary, beyond $50bn with Feynman per the body), with strength also in AVGO and memory. NVDA is the best risk/reward as the market questions 2027 AI capex, at 15x FY28 EPS.

In a pause, MS would expect the most disruption at the tail of the bullwhip: memory, optics and small-dollar components such as power management and analog that are most likely to be over-ordered. Analog and GFS now have material AI revenue.

MS expects the memory cycle to enter its late stage in 4Q26 but not end. Price increases moderate, inventories rise and supply grows, limiting earnings surprises. Memory stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E. Stocks have historically turned about four months before y/y pricing peaks.

Part of the recent capex raises reflects component costs, not volume. Amazon's CFO attributed most of its capex lift from $200B to about $220B to rising memory costs, so memory price is a swing factor in the $1.6T figure.

Networking captures about $0.25 of incremental networking revenue per incremental capex dollar, and about $0.15 from hyperscalers and neoclouds. Hyperscaler-linked networking revenue across 15 companies grows from $62.6B in CY25 to $141B in CY26E and $237B in CY27E. A 10-point change in hyperscaler share moves CY27E revenue by about $38bn.

In tech hardware, DELL (EW) is forecast at about $6.6B of gross profit from T2 CSPs and neoclouds in CY27 on about $123B of revenue. HPE (OW) is at about $2.1B of gross profit, SNX (OW) about $1.5B via Hyve, and P (OW) about $700M of hyperscale revenue. STX and WDC (both OW) have roughly 60% of revenue tied to US hyperscalers, about $30B in CY27.

For Taiwan ODMs, ODM value-add is only a mid-single-digit share of rack ASP. MS models value-add per rack up 35-40% on VR200 versus GB300 while rack ASP almost doubles. Consensus has Big Four CSP capex growth moderating from about 90% in 2026 to about 42% in 2027 and about 11% in 2028, and ODMs trade below their 20-year average 2027E P/E of 11.5x.

In EDA, Synopsys and Cadence have underperformed the market YTD on 'AI disrupted' fears, which MS thinks are overdone. Synopsys' new royalty-based application-optimised IP model raises sensitivity to hyperscaler custom silicon volumes. EDA demand is more tied to design programmes than shipment volumes.

In multi-industry, VRT (OW) is about 90% data center exposed and ETN about 33%. FPS (EW) is about 65%, TT and JCI about 20%, CARR about 12% and HUBB about 8%. Backlogs cover the bulk of 2027. The debate is 2030 durability, chiller content, 800V DC architecture and disintermediation by hyperscalers.

In machinery, MS ranks EROC as most levered to hyperscaler spend, followed by CMI and CAT, on onsite and backup power. Large-displacement engines are sold out through at least 1H28. Second-order beneficiaries include construction equipment, aggregates and Target Hospitality (TH).

In power, GEV gas turbines are sold out through 2029 at about $3,000/kW versus $1,000/kW in the early 2020s. OEMs require 20-40% deposits and are taking orders out to 2032. MS expects a flight to quality toward tier-one suppliers GEV, INIO and BE.

Hyperscalers have issued about $255B of unsecured bonds YTD, about 30% of estimated 2026 capex. Cash-flow deficits peak in 2027. High-quality hyperscalers (AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT) have interest coverage of 30.7x in 2026 and 11.9x pro forma in 2027. Lower-quality ones (ORCL, SPCX) fall from 4.0x to 1.8x.

Neoclouds rely on asset-level financing and convertibles and are the most sensitive to a higher cost of debt. MS expects 2027 issuance to skew toward shorter-duration unsecured paper and asset-backed financing, concentrated in the US IG market.

Risks to the downside include a compounding volume and price decline (the late-2022 memory analog saw NAND shipments fall about 5% while prices fell 20-30%) and a US power shortfall of 32 GW through 2028 (34% of 97 GW needed). Data-center policy is another risk, with state and local restrictions a midterm election wedge issue and a Republican sweep seen as the most constructive outcome.
Upside risks include Wall Street underestimating secular compute cycles by an average of 38%, persistent bottlenecks and faster AI adoption.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscaler investment continues to favor large-cap semis (NVDA, AVGO, memory). Multiples have compressed since the July peaks, so upward capex revisions could address cycle-longevity concerns.

The cycle is in its late stage from 4Q26 with moderating price increases and rising supply. Stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E, and the main downside is a hyperscaler capex plateau hitting pricing before volume.
Power constraints favor onsite generation and high-quality equipment suppliers. Backlogs are extended and upward capex revisions would lengthen them at higher margins.
DELL, HPE, SNX, STX, WDC and P are the main conduits of hyperscaler capex into revenue and profit.
Custom silicon investment broadens the opportunity for SNPS and CDNS. The AI-disruption fear is considered overdone.

earnings_insights: MS expects SPX 2027 net income growth of 12% (36% in 2026), with AI names at 25% and SPX ex-AI at 4%. Earnings growth peaked in 2Q26 for both cohorts (consensus-based, FactSet).
Hon Hai: cloud and networking were 51% of 2Q26 sales and August 2026 sales rose 52% y/y to NT$921.8B (reported). Management guided AI rack shipments to more than double in 2026.
Quanta: servers were over 80% of 2Q26 sales and AI is 75-80% of that line. 2026 AI server revenue is guided to double (company guidance).
Eaton data center business is up 50%+ y/y YTD. Forgent data center business grew 161% in F26, and management guided total F27 revenue up 76% (company guidance).
MS forecasts Dell at about $123B of CY27 revenue from T2 CSPs and neoclouds and about $6.6B of gross profit (MS estimates, not reported).
Consensus has Big Four CSP capex growth moderating from about 90% y/y this year to about 42% in 2027 and about 11% in 2028 (consensus estimates).

trade_ideas.description: Long NVDA as best risk/reward in semis into the 2027 AI capex debate
trade_ideas.rationale: The stock trades at 15x FY28 EPS and numbers keep going up, with multiple expansion upside if AI enthusiasm returns.
trade_ideas.risk: A power bottleneck or an AI capex slowdown could hit chip orders.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight power and electrical equipment suppliers (GEV, INIO, BE) as a flight to quality
trade_ideas.rationale: Backlogs are filled through 2028 with 20-40% deposits, and tier-one suppliers are the most de-risked.
trade_ideas.risk: A demand downturn would soften pricing and utilization, with newer entrants hit hardest.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight bottleneck and share-gain beneficiaries as capex growth moderates into 2028
trade_ideas.rationale: These companies should keep seeing upward revenue and earnings revisions even if hyperscaler capex revisions moderate.

risk_factors: Power bottleneck: a 32 GW net US shortfall through 2028 could delay chip deployment and strand inventory.
A compounding volume and price decline once capacity catches up, as in the late-2022 memory downturn.
A plateau in hyperscaler capex would hit memory pricing before volume.
Financing constraints for lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds as cash-flow deficits peak in 2027.
Data center policy and election risk at the state and local level.
Disintermediation by hyperscalers insourcing power and cooling products.
Optical oversupply and falling optical content per unit of bandwidth.
Execution risk on supplier capacity expansions, as seen at ETN and VRT.
The $1.6T estimate assumes every chip ordered gets powered and put to work.

vol_and_positioning: Semiconductor multiples have compressed since the July peaks, and memory stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E.
ODMs trade at a 2027E P/E below their 20-year average of 11.5x.

geopolitical: Data center restrictions are a midterm election wedge issue. State and local policy in TX, OH, PA, GA, NV, WI, MI, AZ and LA is the binding lever, and MS does not expect a federal pause.
Export controls and domestic Chinese competition are flagged as risks for EDA companies.
CXMT raised about US$8.6bn in its July STAR Market IPO to fund memory wafer capacity and is modeled entering HBM from 2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex estimates have been repeatedly revised higher, and Wall Street has underestimated compute cycles by about 38% on average. ROIC of 25-50% supports continued investment, and bottlenecks keep pricing power intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex growth slows to about 14% in 2028, financing needs and cash-flow deficits peak in 2027, and a power shortfall could strand inventory. Volume and price could fall together, as in the 2022 memory downturn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slippage in energization (the 32 GW US power shortfall) forcing chip orders to be pushed out, or a plateau in hyperscaler capex hitting memory pricing before volume.

tension_points.bull_case: DRAM is a key bottleneck, long-term agreements cover most demand and stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Price increases moderate from 4Q26, inventories rise and supply grows, including from CXMT. Strong forward buying could reverse quickly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rollover in y/y contract price growth, with stocks historically turning about four months before the pricing peak.

tension_points.bull_case: Backlogs cover the bulk of 2027, project announcements and pipeline commentary support durability through 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Bottlenecks in power, labor and supply chain, plus uncertainty around projects yet to break ground. Backlogs typically stretch only about 18 months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New supplier capacity normalizing lead times and capex downturns driven by reduced hyperscaler and utility spending.
